arc: networkd: DeviceManager listens to all shill events always. Previously, arc-networkd would register/unregister shill handlers when ARC++ booted up or shut down, respectively. But in a multi-guest world, it needs to be aware of the host devices independent of guest lifecyles. And more specifically, for ARCVM it needs to be aware at VM boot time. *** This is a reland of https://crrev.com/c/1707790 *** BUG=b:133193765 TEST=units Change-Id: I6c95315b157e26ed450144909725b973f820623f Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1828658 Tested-by: Garrick Evans <garrick@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Garrick Evans <garrick@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: ChromeOS CL Exonerator Bot <chromiumos-cl-exonerator@appspot.gserviceaccount.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hugo Benichi <hugobenichi@google.com> Reviewed-by: Taoyu Li <taoyl@chromium.org>

arc: networkd: Move setup and teardown logic into ArcService. This patch refactors the setup/teardown, init/uninit and enable/disable code from ArcIpConfig into ArcService. Earlier attempts to break each logical unit into multicle CLs caused too many problems given the timing and interconencted nature of these pieces, due largely to the fact that the functionality was beig split across processes. Another key change in this patch is the gating of enable/disable on both sides of the veth pair being up. This is achieved by DeviceManager listening to rt netlink messages on the host and ArcService doing the same in the container's net namespace. Doing so, guarantees that once IPv6 route detection and address assignment runs, it can set up the datapath and configuration immediately. One caveat here is that the device keeps state that is currently specific to the ARC guest alone. This will have to be expanded, if necessary, to accomodate others. More functionality is moved into Datapath from ArcIpConfig. In order to add DeviceManager unit testing, a base class was added for mocking. ArcIpConfig unit test removed since it is no longer relevant. TODO: Add relevant tests to ArcSeviceTest *** This is a reland of https://crrev.com/c/1727633 but with the following fixes: (1) Devices are created once (as before) rather than repeated created and destroyed whenever the ArcService starts and stops. This is necessary to prevent shill from crashing when the virtual (wifi?) device is recreated (https://crbug.com/1008686). (2) The Android device is not added by default in DeviceManager but rather explicitly by the ArcService first starts. (3) ARC N boards not being enabled when the device manager detects the link is up. attestation: migrate to generalized MOCK_METHOD() macro This CL replaces the uses of MOCK_METHOD*() and MOCK_CONST_METHOD*() macros in unit tests with the generalized MOCK_METHOD() macro, which is now the recommended way to define mocked methods with gmock. In particular, MOCK_METHOD() supports annotating a mocked method with specifiers such as 'override'. One minor change is that argument names are omitted in the argument list provided to MOCK_METHOD() in order to prevent clang-format from formatting code like `Foo* foo` into `Foo * foo`. init: fix incorrect result from GetBlockCount The GetBlockCount helper function falls back to checking /sys/class/block/[dev]/size to get a count of blocks if dumpe2fs fails. However, that interface returns a count of sectors (512 bytes) instead of blocks (often 4096 bytes). This means that if we do get the block count from this fallback, our count will be 8 times too large. This causes an error message when we attempt to write beyond the size of the file system. Add block size as a parameter to GetBlockCount, so that we can convert the sector count into a block count. cryptohome: Expose mount operations in a single function. In order to move cryptohome mount operations out of process, first we need to expose them as a single function in the helper. The reason for this is pretty straightforward: when executing out of process, the helper needs to be able to carry out all the mount operations in a single invocation. The easiest way to ensure that this will be possible is to perform all mount operations as a result of a single function invocation. Then we change the function invocation to a helper executable invocation and we're done. This continues the work in the previous CL by transferring enough state to the MountHelper class to allow regular user mounts to be completed with a single call to the helper. In order to make the helper API less overly verbose, this CL also introduces an Options struct for the helper. As opposed to ephemeral mounts, where the entire *Inner function could be moved to the helper, for regular mounts the *Inner function does quite a bit of key manipulation. Per the design these should stay in cryptohome and not be done in the helper, so for regular mounts the helper calls happen inside of the *Inner function instead of fully replacing it. This is not a big deal since seam between the Mount class and the helper is still pretty obvious since key operations happen first and mount operations happen later. The next CL in the series will move unmount calls to the helper, in preparation for running things out of process (this is the plan at https://docs.google.com/document/d/1hSUSuIQLZvH1OVwn7N8lDIT7lFUEeHkmFDXQduBccho/edit#.) This CL is a net addition of fewer than 100 lines. Most of it is code moved around. BUG=chromium:985492 TEST=Unit tests pass. TEST=Add new user to Chromebook successfully. TEST=Log in, create local data, log out. TEST=Log back in, local data is still present. UPSTREAM: Bluetooth: btrtl: HCI reset on close for Realtek BT chip Realtek RTL8822BE BT chip on ASUS X420FA cannot be turned on correctly after on-off several times. Bluetooth daemon sets BT mode failed when this issue happens. Scanning must be active while turning off for this bug to be hit. bluetoothd[1576]: Failed to set mode: Failed (0x03) If BT is turned off, then turned on again, it works correctly again. According to the vendor driver, the HCI_QUIRK_RESET_ON_CLOSE flag is set during probing. So, this patch makes Realtek's BT reset on close to fix this issue.
